aids.description_en: Conditional cash transfer program for poor and vulnerable families. Components: pregnant/nursing mothers (Rp 750,000/year), children under 6 (Rp 750,000/year), school children SD (Rp 900,000/year), SMP (Rp 1,500,000/year), SMA (Rp 2,000,000/year), elderly 70+ (Rp 2,400,000/year), disabled severe (Rp 2,400,000/year). Total up to Rp 3,000,000/year per family. Paid quarterly via KKS (Electronic Welfare Card). Source: kemensos.go.id.

Non-cash food assistance of Rp 200,000/month disbursed as e-voucher (KKS) redeemable at registered warung/agent for food staples (rice, eggs, etc.). Targets 18.8 million poor households (DTKS registry). Source: kemensos.go.id.

Student scholarship for poor children: SD/MI (primary school) Rp 450,000/year; SMP/MTs (junior high) Rp 750,000/year; SMA/SMK (senior high) Rp 1,000,000/year. Disbursed via BRI/BSI bank accounts. Source: kemdikbud.go.id.
aids.organisme: Kementerian Pendidikan, Kebudayaan, Riset dan Teknologi

aids.description_en: Vocational training program for unemployed/underemployed workers. Total benefit Rp 3,550,000 per participant: training incentive Rp 2,500,000 (for online courses on partner platforms) + post-training incentive Rp 600,000/month x 2 months + survey incentive Rp 50,000 x 3. Source: prakerja.go.id.

aids.nom: Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional — Penerima Bantuan Iuran (JKN-PBI)
aids.description_en: Free national health insurance (BPJS Kesehatan) for poor and vulnerable households. Premium paid by central government (Rp 0 for PBI beneficiaries). Covers primary care at puskesmas/clinic and hospital referrals. Source: bpjs-kesehatan.go.id.

Electricity tariff subsidy for household connections 450 VA (lowest income, fully subsidized) and 900 VA (subsidized — households with per capita income below Rp 1,400,000/month). The 450 VA tariff is Rp 415/kWh versus normal rate Rp 1,699/kWh. Source: esdm.go.id / PLN.

Direct cash transfer of Rp 300,000/month for poor households affected by economic shocks (fuel subsidy adjustment, inflation, disasters). Disbursed through post offices (Kantor Pos) or village funds (Dana Desa). Available on a periodic basis as policy response. Source: kemensos.go.id.

Cash-for-work program paying Rp 100,000/day for unskilled poor workers on public infrastructure projects (roads, irrigation, village infrastructure). Implemented through village funds and various ministries. Minimum 5 working days per participant per project. Source: pu.go.id.

Subsidized housing mortgage with fixed 5% interest rate over loan term (up to 20 years). Maximum home price Rp 166,000,000 (type 36). Down payment minimum 1%. Maximum borrower income Rp 8,000,000/month (non-subsidized area). Source: kemenpera / pupr.go.id.

Old-age savings plan through BPJS Ketenagakerjaan. Employer contributes 3.7% and employee 2% of salary per month. Lump-sum disbursement at retirement (age 56+), permanent disability, or death. Average accumulation depends on salary and tenure. Source: bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id.

Work accident insurance. Covers medical costs (100%) for work-related injuries, temporary disability benefit (100% salary for first 12 months, 75% thereafter), permanent disability up to 70% of base pay x 80 months, and death benefit. Funded by employer contribution 0.24-1.74% of salary. Source: bpjsketenagakerjaan.go.id.

Social assistance for persons with severe disabilities not covered by family: Rp 300,000/month (non-PKH recipients). Distributed via Post Office. Managed by Ministry of Social Affairs. Source: kemensos.go.id.
